query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor addition of a large-atomic-size element (e.g., 3–5 at.% zirconium) into phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys will enhance their glass‐forming ability and increase the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.material_initial_state: A phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy in its conventional (non‐modified) formulation, which shows limited glass forming ability and low amorphous thermal stability.
generation.intervention: Adjust the alloy composition by substituting a small fraction (e.g., 3–5 at.%) of one of the constituent elements with zirconium.
generation.conditions: Rapid quenching under inert atmosphere to form the amorphous phase; the intervention is expected to be effective under processing conditions that avoid significant oxidation or phase segregation.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced atomic size mismatch and increased local chemical disorder due to the presence of zirconium.
generation.mechanism: The added zirconium disrupts long‐range atomic ordering by increasing viscosity and kinetic barriers to nucleation. This delays crystallization upon heating and thus improves both the glass‐forming ability during processing and the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the control alloy, the zirconium-modified alloy will exhibit a higher amorphous volume fraction when rapidly quenched and a higher crystallization onset temperature (indicative of improved thermal stability).
generation.baseline: Phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy without any zirconium addition processed under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement is anticipated only when the overall alloy chemistry supports an amorphous structure; if the base alloy has insufficient phosphorus content or if processing conditions permit significant phase segregation, the intervention may not yield the expected benefits.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal zirconium concentration and the magnitude of improvement in glass-forming ability and thermal stability may depend on subtle compositional and processing details that require systematic exploration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys with a minor 3–5 at.% zirconium substitution and a control set without zirconium. Process both sets using identical rapid quenching methods under inert atmosphere to achieve an amorphous structure. Characterize the samples using X-ray diffraction and differential scanning calorimetry.
measurements: X-ray diffraction to quantify the amorphous vs. crystalline phase fraction
Differential scanning calorimetry to determine the crystallization onset temperatures
Microscopy (e.g., TEM) to assess the nanoscale structure and uniformity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the zirconium-doped alloy does not consistently show a statistically significant increase in the amorphous phase fraction and a higher crystallization onset temperature compared to the control alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
